title: CPIC phenotype vocabulary, CYP2D6 activity-score bands and conditional notes
licence: CPIC guideline content is dedicated to the public domain under CC0. Phenotype terms follow the CPIC/DPWG standardised terms for pharmacogenetic phenotype nomenclature; 'extensive metabolizer' is DEPRECATED and does not appear. Activity-score bands for CYP2D6 follow Caudle and co-workers, Clinical and Translational Science (2020), 'Standardizing CYP2D6 genotype to phenotype translation'.
boundaryStatement: These are CONDITIONAL NOTES about what a phenotype would imply. BioCAD does not interpret a genotype, does not assign a phenotype, and emits no dose or dose adjustment. Consult the CPIC guideline and a clinician for anything actionable.

notes.implication: CPIC states that in a CYP2D6 poor metabolizer the O-demethylation of codeine to morphine is greatly reduced, so the analgesic effect attributed to morphine is expected to be reduced.
CPIC states that in a CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizer the conversion of codeine to morphine is increased, which has been associated with toxicity reports.
CPIC states that formation of the active O-desmethyl metabolite is reduced in a CYP2D6 poor metabolizer.
CPIC states that formation of the active O-desmethyl metabolite is increased in a CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizer.
CPIC states that atomoxetine exposure is higher in a CYP2D6 poor metabolizer than in a normal metabolizer.

CYP2D6 is the principal route of dextromethorphan O-demethylation, so the parent/metabolite ratio differs by phenotype; dextromethorphan is a standard CYP2D6 probe substrate in the FDA interaction tables.
CPIC states that bioactivation of clopidogrel is reduced in a CYP2C19 poor metabolizer, giving lower active-metabolite exposure.
CPIC states that a CYP2C19 intermediate metabolizer also has reduced active-metabolite formation relative to a normal metabolizer.
CPIC states that proton-pump-inhibitor exposure is increased in a CYP2C19 poor metabolizer.
CPIC states that proton-pump-inhibitor exposure is decreased in a CYP2C19 rapid metabolizer.
Amphetamine is a CYP2D6 substrate in part; CPIC publishes no amphetamine guideline, so this is a substrate note and NOT a CPIC recommendation.

Caffeine is predominantly a CYP1A2 substrate. CPIC publishes no CYP1A2/caffeine guideline, and CYP1A2 activity is strongly environmentally modulated (smoking induction), so no phenotype-based statement is made here.
